images.caption: Panas Kravtsov (1909-1974) veteran of Winter war and WW2, twice captured by the Germans, after the war he was separated from his family and exiled to Kamchatka. Son of Damien Kravtsov (died in 1921 during the first Soviet famine) and Lukia Stachenko (1879-1973) who helped fellow villagers during the Holodomor 1932-1933 and Znamianka partisans during the Nazi occupation. Before World War II he worked in the city of Znamianka as a shoemaker. He had a son Dmytro (1932-1946) who died from the consequences of the war and the last Soviet famine, an older daughter Vira (1935-2011) and a younger daughter Lidia (born in 1938)

images.caption: Экспонат Сахаровского центра в Москве: географическая карта, на которой показаны дислокация спецкомендатур, места расселения и численность депортированных в Киргизию немцев, чеченцев, ингушей, балкарцев, карачаевцев, калмыков, крымских татар и выселенцев из Грузии на 20 декабря 1948 года (копия карты из Государственного архива РФ). На карте стоит гриф «Совершенно секретно». Фотосъёмка карты сделана в конце октября 2019 года. 18 августа 2023 года (во время полномасштабной войны против Украины) путинский режим ликвидировал Сахаровский центр.

images.caption:
Moscow Summer of 1976
At the moment (in 2018) this is the most viewed photograph in my Flickr account that is one I took.  Oddly, I have no recollection of taking this photograph, but I did make a brief visit to Moscow where apparently I took this.  Other than that it was in Moscow (which would have been noted on the slide frame, and not from memory) I have no idea where this was in Moscow.

I had a basic Pentax 35 mm camera and did not have any kind of telephoto lens, so this was taken not very far away.  Apparently I would just wait until it seemed no one was looking my way and shoot.  For a (obvious) foreigner to be taking a photo of a scene like this would not be received with much pleasure.

images.filename: Main entrance of the Memento Park with Lenin, Marx and Engels.JPG
images.caption: The main entrance to the Memento Park, designed by architect Ákos Eleőd, is shapped in the image of a monumental classicist building. On its left stands a 4 meter high Lenin statue, previously in the Dozsa Gyorgy street, while on its right stands the cubist Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels granit monument which once stood at the main entrance of the communist party head quarters in Budapest, in the central square Jászai Mari tér.
